title: Scalar Variables - Text
description: MENTOR-9: "Variables are how robots store information. Let's start with scalar variables—single values like text, numbers, or status codes."

story.setup: The ship's systems are coming online, but MENTOR-9 notices something.
story.context: "PROTO-7, we need to track system status. We can't hardcode values everywhere—what if the ship name changes? What if we need to reuse information? That's where variables come in."
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! You've stored text in variables and reused them. This is fundamental—variables let us write flexible, maintainable code. No more repeating the same text everywhere!"

instructions: Create a test case named 'Ship Information'
Create a scalar variable named '${ship_name}' with value 'SYNTAX-IV Explorer'
Create a scalar variable named '${status}' with value 'operational'
Create a scalar variable named '${captain}' with value 'MENTOR-9'
Log the ship name with message: 'Ship: SYNTAX-IV Explorer'
Log the status with message: 'Status: operational'
Log the captain with message: 'Captain: MENTOR-9'
Run the code and inspect the Console tab to see variable values
hints: Use 'Set Variable' keyword to create scalar variables
Variables can be used in text by referencing them with ${} notation

theory.title: Scalar Variables: Storing Text
theory.content:
The ship's diagnostic panel flickers. MENTOR-9 points to a repeating pattern in the logs.

MENTOR-9: "See that? We're typing 'SYNTAX-IV Explorer' twelve times. What if we need to change the ship name? We'd have to update it everywhere. That's inefficient and error-prone. We need variables."

What Are Scalar Variables?

A scalar variable stores a single value—like a label on a storage box. You put something in, and you can take it out later by referencing the label.

In Robot Framework:

  • Create a variable with the 'Set Variable' keyword
  • Name it with ${} syntax: ${variable_name}
  • Use it anywhere by referencing the name

The Pattern

*** Test Cases ***
Example
    ${variable_name}    Set Variable    value goes here
    Log    Using variable: ${variable_name}

How it works:

  1. Line 1: 'Set Variable' creates the variable and stores the value
  2. Line 2: ${variable_name} is replaced with the stored value when used

Why Use Variables?

  • Reusability: Define once, use many times
  • Maintainability: Change in one place, updates everywhere
  • Clarity: Named variables are more meaningful than raw values
  • Flexibility: Easy to modify test data without changing test logic

Variable Naming Rules

  • Must start with ${ and end with }
  • Can contain letters, numbers, underscores
  • Case-insensitive (${name} = ${NAME} = ${Name})
  • Descriptive names are better: ${ship_status} not ${s}

Text Variables in Action

${greeting}    Set Variable    Hello, robot!
Log    ${greeting}
Log    Message: ${greeting}
Log    ${greeting} How are you?

All three logs will display the greeting text. The variable is replaced with its value wherever it appears.
